cells.tense: Quietly you can feel what is fair without working it out, and you end what has run its course without a fight.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Take something you ended rather than kept alive, and set beside it what it left you — a skill, a room of your own, a truth.
cells.core:
In the body's held strength, the weighing has gone quiet. You can feel what is fair the way you feel a room's temperature — no tally, no case to build. What has run its course in your body you end without a fight, and the ending leaves something in your hands rather than taking.

So gather what the change grew. Take something you ended rather than kept alive, and set beside it what it left you — a skill, a room of your own, a truth. The counting is not the old accounting; it is standing in a harvest. No one has to agree with your verdict for the fruit to be real, and if some of it is yours alone, that is how a harvest comes in — in private, first. What you gather here feeds what opens next.
cells.sheetLine: Your sense of what's fair knows how to end well.
cells.verb: Weighing what was spilled against what still stands.
cells.place: Standing in the body's held strength under pressure.

cells.tense: Already you are bracing for what fairness will cost before it has asked, and the account runs ahead of the deed.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Someone is weighed down by a task this week — carry it for them, and when it's finished, be finished.
cells.core:
Bracing is what strength does when it runs ahead. The private compass starts weighing a wrong that hasn't happened, working out what will be owed before the day has asked, and the body under it carries that as load. The strength is real — it is the same thing that holds form — but it has turned inward as pre-emptive accounting, and it wears.

Help is the other direction, and it is the same strength. Someone is weighed down by a task this week — carry it for them, and when it's finished, be finished. Finishing is part of it: help that closes teaches the body that an account can close. One deed in a hand, signed off. What you carry in advance goes out to someone instead, and lands.
cells.sheetLine: The scale is running ahead of a day that hasn't asked yet.
cells.verb: Weighing what was spilled against what still stands.
cells.place: Standing in the body's held strength under pressure.

cells.tense: The compass went still a while back, and the direction it once pointed at is no longer in motion.
cells.act: point to the passage you can see
cells.ask: Where you once got through something hard, name the turn that got you out, once, and stop there.
cells.core:
The compass is still in the body. You know how to bear weight — it is there in the hands — but what it once pointed at is no longer moving, and a still compass is not a wrong one. What is empty is the showing.

Point to the passage you can see. Where you once got through something hard, name the turn that got you out, once, and stop there. The words are yours, and they do not need to be complete to be directions: you walked it once, so you can point. You are not pushing anyone, and you are not pushing yourself. Solitude used to connect you to something; this is that connection, handed over. Then it is theirs.
cells.sheetLine: You know the route. You've stopped pointing at it.
cells.verb: Weighing what was spilled against what still stands.

cells.tense: The fairness you are already living is written in your days, and your hand stays off the page.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: List the standards you judge yourself against, then mark the ones you actually hold — those are the ones you answer to.
cells.core:
You are already living a fairness in the body — holding what is held, carrying what is carried — and your account of it says things came that way. The compass is running; the pen is down. The verdicts you hand down are sound, and the verdicts you were handed are filed as your own.

So sort what is yours from what you borrowed. List the standards you judge yourself against, then mark the ones you actually hold — those are the ones you answer to. The borrowed ones can stay, or go. The list is not a court; it is a sorting. What remains marked is a compass signed by the one who used it.
cells.sheetLine: The sense of what's fair is running. You're not signing it.
cells.verb: Weighing what was spilled against what still stands.
cells.place: Standing in the body's held strength under pressure.
